title: Search Race
body:
Goal: write binary search and race it against linear search by counting steps (how many items each one looks at).

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny. Read linear_search - it is done.
  2. Finish binary_search using the steps in the TODO.
  3. Press Run. You should see:
Searching for the LAST number in a sorted list:
   items |  linear |  binary
      10 |      10 |       4
     100 |     100 |       7
    1000 |    1000 |      10
   10000 |   10000 |      14

Extra: add 100000 to the list of sizes. How many steps does each need? Why does binary search only work on a SORTED list?

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read linear_search first. It counts steps and returns two things. binary_search must return the same two things. Look at the TODO steps and picture a loop that keeps going while there is still something left to search.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Use a while loop with low and high. Each time around, count one step, find the middle with //, and compare. A match returns right away. Otherwise move low or high so half of the list is thrown away.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Keep looping while low ____ high:. Add 1 to steps, then find mid = (____ + ____) // 2. Use if, elif and else on items[mid]. If it is too small, set low = ____. If it is too big, set high = ____.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Search Race - YOUR version
# Two ways to find something in a list, and a step counter to compare them.
# A "step" = one time we look at an item and compare it with the target.
# Finish the TODOs, then press Run and see if it does what the README says.


def linear_search(items, target):
    """Look at the items one by one, from the start.
    Return (index, steps). index is -1 if the target is not there.
    (Already done - read it first!)"""
    steps = 0
    for index in range(len(items)):
        steps = steps + 1
        if items[index] == target:
            return index, steps
    return -1, steps


def binary_search(items, target):
    """items MUST be sorted. Look in the middle and throw away half each time.
    Return (index, steps). index is -1 if the target is not there."""
    low = 0
    high = len(items) - 1
    steps = 0
    # TODO: while low <= high:
    #           add 1 to steps
    #           mid = (low + high) // 2
    #           if items[mid] == target: return mid, steps
    #           elif items[mid] < target: low = mid + 1
    #           else: high = mid - 1
    return -1, steps


def race(size, target):
    """Search for target in the sorted list 1..size both ways.
    Return (linear_steps, binary_steps)."""
    items = list(range(1, size + 1))
    _, linear_steps = linear_search(items, target)
    _, binary_steps = binary_search(items, target)
    return linear_steps, binary_steps


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Searching for the LAST number in a sorted list:")
    print(f"{'items':>8} | {'linear':>7} | {'binary':>7}")
    for size in [10, 100, 1000, 10000]:
        linear_steps, binary_steps = race(size, size)
        print(f"{size:>8} | {linear_steps:>7} | {binary_steps:>7}")
